gram.d: 祝 launches any blessing: 祝妳生日快樂 happy birthday, 祝你順利 good luck, 祝您身體健康 good health. The all-purpose well-wishing frame — cakes, emails, toasts.

gram.d: 受歡迎 = to be well-received/popular: 最受歡迎的口味 the most popular flavor. 受 flips the verb passive — 受歡迎, 受注意, 受影響 — a formal-leaning pattern you'll meet constantly in news.

scenarios.intro: The moment itself: wish her well, hand over the gift, deflect the age question like a gentleman, and get her to the cake.

turns.task: Drop the act — wish her a happy birthday!

turns.task: Of course! Hand over the gift — this is for you.

scenarios.intro: Tonight's OPI drill: defend business gift-giving, draw the line against bribery, and define what makes a gift right — the exact cultural theory behind tomorrow's pineapple cakes.

them.zh: 在商業場合送禮，你覺得有必要嗎？
them.py: Zài shāngyè chǎnghé sònglǐ, nǐ juéde yǒu bìyào ma?
them.en: Is gift-giving in business settings necessary, in your view?

turns.task: Yes, in Taiwan's context — it's not about the object; it opens the relationship and signals respect.

ans.zh: 在台灣的商業文化裡，我認為有必要。重點不是東西本身，而是打開關係、表達尊重。
ans.py: Zài Táiwān de shāngyè wénhuà lǐ, wǒ rènwéi yǒu bìyào. Zhòngdiǎn búshì dōngxi běnshēn, érshì dǎkāi guānxì, biǎodá zūnzhòng.
ans.en: In Taiwan's business culture, yes. It's not about the object — it opens the relationship and expresses respect.

them.zh: 可是送禮跟賄賂的界線在哪裡？
them.py: Kěshì sònglǐ gēn huìlù de jièxiàn zài nǎlǐ?
them.en: But where's the line between gifting and bribery?

turns.task: Sharp answer: value and intent — a modest gift given openly builds trust; an expensive one given secretly buys favors. Government work makes this line critical.

ans.zh: 界線在價值跟目的：公開送的小禮物是建立信任，偷偷送的貴重禮物是買好處。跟政府做生意，這條線特別重要。
ans.py: Jièxiàn zài jiàzhí gēn mùdì: gōngkāi sòng de xiǎo lǐwù shì jiànlì xìnrèn, tōutōu sòng de guìzhòng lǐwù shì mǎi hǎochù. Gēn zhèngfǔ zuò shēngyì, zhè tiáo xiàn tèbié zhòngyào.
ans.en: The line is value and intent: a modest, open gift builds trust; a pricey, secret one buys favors. In government business that line is critical.

them.zh: 那什麼樣的禮物才「對」？
them.py: Nà shénme yàng de lǐwù cái 'duì'?
them.en: So what makes a gift 'right'?

turns.task: Three tests: local character, shareable by the team, and priced so no one owes anyone — that's why pineapple cakes always win.

ans.zh: 三個條件：有在地特色、整個團隊可以分享、價格不會讓對方有壓力。所以鳳梨酥永遠是正確答案。
ans.py: Sān ge tiáojiàn: yǒu zàidì tèsè, zhěngge tuánduì kěyǐ fēnxiǎng, jiàgé bú huì ràng duìfāng yǒu yālì. Suǒyǐ fènglísū yǒngyuǎn shì zhèngquè dá'àn.
ans.en: Three tests: local character, shareable with the whole team, and a price that pressures nobody. Which is why pineapple cakes are always the right answer.

them.zh: 年輕世代好像越來越不在意這些傳統了？
them.py: Niánqīng shìdài hǎoxiàng yuèláiyuè bú zàiyì zhèxiē chuántǒng le?
them.en: Younger generations seem to care less about these traditions?

turns.task: Concede forms are simplifying, but argue the core survives: 心意 just changes shape — a handwritten card can outweigh a gift box.

ans.zh: 形式確實在簡化，但是核心沒有變：心意只是換了樣子，有時候一張手寫卡片比禮盒更有力量。
ans.py: Xíngshì quèshí zài jiǎnhuà, dànshì héxīn méiyǒu biàn: xīnyì zhǐshì huàn le yàngzi, yǒushíhòu yì zhāng shǒuxiě kǎpiàn bǐ lǐhé gèng yǒu lìliàng.
ans.en: The forms are simplifying, but the core survives — the thought just changes shape. Sometimes a handwritten card beats any gift box.

them.zh: 明天聽說你要去見大客戶？祝你順利！
them.py: Míngtiān tīngshuō nǐ yào qù jiàn dà kèhù? Zhù nǐ shùnlì!
them.en: I hear you're meeting a big client tomorrow? Good luck!

turns.task: Thank the host — tomorrow you'll practice everything discussed tonight, pineapple cakes in hand.

ans.zh: 謝謝！明天我就帶著鳳梨酥，把今天講的理論全部實踐一次！
ans.py: Xièxie! Míngtiān wǒ jiù dàizhe fènglísū, bǎ jīntiān jiǎng de lǐlùn quánbù shíjiàn yícì!
ans.en: Thanks! Tomorrow I put tonight's whole theory into practice — pineapple cakes in hand!

x: 祝你生日快樂！
Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè!
Happy birthday to you!
vocab.n: 過生日 = to have/celebrate a birthday. The song melody is the same one you know.

x: 我們買一個蛋糕慶祝吧！
Wǒmen mǎi yíge dàngāo qìngzhù ba!
Let's get a cake to celebrate!
vocab.n: Sizes run in 吋 (inches): 六吋 serves ~4, 八吋 serves ~10.

vocab.e: to give (a gift); to see someone off; to deliver
x: 這是送你的！
Zhè shì sòng nǐ de!
This is for you!
vocab.n: Triple-duty verb: 送禮物 give gifts, 送你回家 walk you home, 外送 food delivery.

x: 你的狗幾歲了？
Nǐ de gǒu jǐ suì le?
How old is your dog?
vocab.n: 幾歲 for kids/casual; adults politely get 請問您貴庚 (rare) — or just don't ask.

x: 這個禮物太貴重了！
Zhège lǐwù tài guìzhòng le!
This gift is too generous!
vocab.n: Polite receiving ritual: protest once (太客氣了), accept with both hands, open later unless invited to.

x: 台灣人聚會很喜歡唱歌。
Táiwān rén jùhuì hěn xǐhuān chànggē.
Taiwanese gatherings love singing.
vocab.n: KTV is a national institution — refusing to sing at least once is nearly impossible.

x: 她最愛巧克力口味的。
Tā zuì ài qiǎokèlì kǒuwèi de.
She loves chocolate flavor the most.
你要什麼口味的？
Nǐ yào shénme kǒuwèi de?
What flavor would you like?
vocab.n: Also personal taste: 很合我的口味 — right up my alley. Different from 味道 (the taste itself).

x: 簽約以後我們要好好慶祝！
Qiānyuē yǐhòu wǒmen yào hǎohǎo qìngzhù!
After signing we're celebrating properly!
謝謝你的邀請！
Xièxie nǐ de yāoqǐng!
Thanks for the invitation!
vocab.n: Formal register; casual inviting is just 約 (我約你吃飯) or the slangy 揪.

x: 我們給她一個大驚喜！
Wǒmen gěi tā yíge dà jīngxǐ!
Let's give her a big surprise!
vocab.n: 驚喜 is the happy kind; 驚嚇 jīngxià is the scary kind. Choose wisely.

x: 這件事要保密喔！
Zhè jiàn shì yào bǎomì o!
Keep this one under wraps!
vocab.n: Party planning today, 保密協定 (NDA) and classified work tomorrow — a word your industry lives on.

x: 明天七點在門口集合。
Míngtiān qī diǎn zài ménkǒu jíhé.
Muster at the entrance at seven tomorrow.
vocab.n: School trips, tour groups, and military formations all run on 集合時間.

x: 開會以前，麻煩你提醒我一下。
Kāihuì yǐqián, máfán nǐ tíxǐng wǒ yíxià.
Please remind me before the meeting.
vocab.n: The polite nudge verb: 小提醒 = a friendly heads-up; 提醒事項 = reminders list.

x: 董事長也會出席明天的會議。
Dǒngshìzhǎng yě huì chūxí míngtiān de huìyì.
The chairman will also attend tomorrow's meeting.
vocab.n: Formal presence — meetings, ceremonies. Casual attendance is just 參加 or 來.

x: 董事長出席表示他們很重視。
Dǒngshìzhǎng chūxí biǎoshì tāmen hěn zhòngshì.
The chairman attending shows they take it seriously.
vocab.n: Top of the org chart; 總經理 = GM/president below. Address as 王董 for extra fluency points.

x: 這個月的業績成長兩成。
Zhège yuè de yèjì chéngzhǎng liǎng chéng.
This month's sales grew 20%.
vocab.n: 衝業績 = pushing to hit numbers — every salesperson's month-end verb.

x: 週年慶的促銷活動開始了。
Zhōuniánqìng de cùxiāo huódòng kāishǐ le.
The anniversary-sale promotions have begun.
vocab.n: 週年慶 (department-store anniversary sales) is Taiwan's Black Friday — 促銷 season incarnate.

x: 電商平台的競爭非常激烈。
Diànshāng píngtái de jìngzhēng fēicháng jīliè.
E-commerce platform competition is fierce.
vocab.n: Short for 電子商務. Taiwan's big ones: momo, PChome, 蝦皮 (Shopee).

x: 節慶帶動了觀光與消費。
Jiéqìng dàidòng le guānguāng yǔ xiāofèi.
Festivals drive tourism and spending.
vocab.n: Umbrella news-word for the whole holiday economy; a specific holiday is a 節日.

x: 他是標準的派對咖，哪裡熱鬧哪裡去。
Tā shì biāozhǔn de pàiduìkā, nǎlǐ rènào nǎlǐ qù.
Total party animal — wherever the action is, he's there.
slang.n: Taiwan: 咖 (from Hokkien kha, 'leg/role') builds people-types — 咖啡咖 coffee person, 邊緣咖 loner. Endlessly productive suffix.

slang.e: read but no reply (left on read)
x: 我邀請他，結果他已讀不回……
Wǒ yāoqǐng tā, jiéguǒ tā yǐdú bùhuí......
I invited him and he left me on read…
slang.n: Taiwan texting culture's deepest wound, born from LINE's read receipts. The passive-aggressive art form.

x: 今晚超鬧熱，整層樓都是我們的人！
Jīnwǎn chāo nāu-jia̍t, zhěng céng lóu dōu shì wǒmen de rén!
Tonight's popping — the whole floor is ours!
slang.n: Hokkien for 熱鬧 (characters flipped!). Temple festivals, night markets, and good parties are all 鬧熱.

slang.e: sense of ceremony — making moments feel special
x: 蠟燭一定要吹，生日要有儀式感！
Làzhú yídìng yào chuī, shēngrì yào yǒu yíshìgǎn!
The candles MUST be blown out — birthdays need ceremony!
slang.n: Mainland internet-born, now pan-Chinese lifestyle vocabulary. The philosophy behind every decorated latte.

x: 促銷一來我就剁手，買了一堆禮物。
Cùxiāo yì lái wǒ jiù duòshǒu, mǎi le yìduī lǐwù.
The sale hit and my hands betrayed me — bought a pile of gifts.
slang.n: Mainland e-commerce slang (Double-11 era): spend so much you vow to chop your hands off. Never actually stops anyone.
